summary:
INFINITY GOM FIRE WATCH SYSTEM is a web application that harmonizes MODIS and VIIRS active fire hotspots (NASA FIRMS) into a single fire activity calendar, from 2000 to the present, for any area of interest.

MODIS (1 km) and VIIRS (375 m) do not count the same fire in the same way, so their records cannot be compared directly. Our application applies a common filter, calibrates both sensors with a per-region regression over the years in which they observed simultaneously, and converts MODIS to the VIIRS scale. The series continues with NOAA-20 after the end of Suomi NPP. For the Dominican Republic the fit reaches R² = 0.89 over 167 months.

Users select a country and province, see the months and years with the highest activity, compare the current month with its historical median, and download the results as CSV. The system also turns data into action: a map of recent hotspots, an estimated fire spread path, evacuation and response routes, email alerts, and an educational dispatch simulator.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

It merges more than two decades of active fire hotspots from MODIS (Terra and Aqua) and VIIRS (Suomi NPP and NOAA-20) into a consistent time series and presents it as a year × month calendar. It shows the critical period, the most active year, the current month's anomaly against its historical median, and the relationship between sensors. Users can compare two years, two months or two days, and MODIS against VIIRS for any period and data type (detections, daytime, nighttime, fire radiative power). The area of interest is chosen by country and province, by drawing a rectangle, or by latitude and longitude. Results can be exported as CSV and as a printable report.

HOW THE HARMONIZATION WORKS

1) Common filter: vegetation fires only; MODIS confidence ≥ 30% and VIIRS nominal or high confidence. 2) Local calibration: log-log regression of monthly counts over the 2012–2026 overlap. 3) A single series on the VIIRS 375 m scale: converted MODIS until 2011, Suomi NPP until November 2026, and calibrated NOAA-20 afterwards. The application displays the fit and its limits: it is a statistical correction and does not recover small fires that MODIS never detected.

BEYOND THE CHALLENGE

A map with recent hotspots and NASA GIBS layers; an estimated fire spread path based on wind and humidity; evacuation, water and response-team routes on real roads; indicative estimates of water needs and response resources; a forecast of critical months and a 7-day risk outlook; email alerts with filters; a public user guide; accessible color themes; and an educational simulator in which an Arduino robot, with prior authorization, represents dispatching a drone or crew to the hotspot's coordinates.

BENEFITS AND IMPACT

It gives early warning services, firefighters, scientists and land managers a consistent view of when and where fires occur, and gives the public a simple answer: whether there is a fire nearby and which way to go.

TOOLS

HTML, CSS and JavaScript in a single page; Leaflet; Python for data preparation; Arduino; EmailJS; Firebase Hosting; GitHub.

FACTORS CONSIDERED

Continuity of the record as Suomi NPP ends and Terra/Aqua approach end of life, accessible color ramps, plain language for non-experts, and transparency about what is NASA data and what is our own estimate.
